item.title: Accelerating the Building of a Healthy China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Accelerating the Building of a Healthy China Accelerating the Building of a Healthy China XI JINPING The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) has made the strategic decision to build a Healthy China by 2035, and the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) is a critical window for achieving this goal. We must take a coordinated approach to planning and press ahead with urgency to secure decisive progress toward this goal. First, medical and health services should be developed in light of China’s realities China is a developing socialist country with a vast population where considerable disparities still persist between urban and rural areas and among regions. These realities dictate that we follow a path of health development with distinctive Chinese characteristics, ensuring that our Party exercises leadership over health work, putting the people and their lives above all else, implementing a health-first strategy, and seeing that basic medical and health services are oriented toward the public interest. At the National Health Conference in 2016, the CPC Central Committee put forward the guidelines for health development in the new era: giving priority to community-level services, using reform and innovation to drive progress, putting prevention first, placing equal emphasis on Western medicine and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), incorporating health considerations into all policies, and ensuring the people contribute to and benefit from the development of health care. The profound achievements in China’s health sector since the advent of the new era in 2012 are ample proof that these guidelines are well-suited to China’s national context and are entirely correct. Both now and in the period ahead, specific health work policies and measures will need to be adjusted and refined in response to changing circumstances. What we must not waver in, however, is our commitment to following the path of health development with Chinese characteristics or implementing the guidelines for health work in the new era. On these fundamental issues, we must remain clear-headed and maintain strategic resolve. General Secretary Xi Jinping visits national political advisors from the Chinese Peasants and Workers Democratic Party, the Jiusan Society, the sector of medicine and health, and the sector of social welfare and social security, who are attending the fourth session of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, Beijing, afternoon of March 6, 2026. Xi attended their joint group meeting to hear their comments and suggestions. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER XIE HUANCHI Second, priority should be placed on key areas in advancing the Healthy China Initiative Building a Healthy China is a systematic endeavor. As people’s medical and healthcare needs grow and diversify, we should focus on what will benefit the population broadly and have a far-reaching impact across the entire health sector. Both our efforts and resources should be concentrated on such tasks to deliver further progress. For instance, improving the public health system requires deepening public participation, strengthening coordination and integration of medical care and disease prevention initiatives, and reinforcing epidemic prevention and control, monitoring and early warning, medical treatment, emergency response, supply provision, and oversight and management. We should also attach great importance to mental health and psychiatric care, strengthening preventive guidance, early detection, and comprehensive intervention. General Secretary Xi Jinping talks with medical staff at the community health station of the CPC-led community service center, Changcheng Huayuan Community, Jinfeng District, Yinchuan City, afternoon of June 19, 2024. Xi visited Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region on an inspection tour on June 19 and 20. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER XIE HUANCHI Another example is meeting the people’s growing expectations for a high-quality and efficient medical service system. We should continue to improve the layout of the system, carry out capacity-building projects for community-level health care, promote tiered diagnosis and treatment, and strengthen operational support for medical and health institutions at the county, district, and community levels. We should also promote integrated application of TCM and Western medicine, shore up weak links in services for key populations and under-resourced specialties, strengthen comprehensive prevention and control of chronic diseases, and expand the provision of services such as rehabilitative care and palliative care. A further example is the promotion of healthy and wholesome lifestyles. In this regard, we need to further raise public health literacy, advance public fitness initiatives and patriotic health campaigns, and guide people to maintain balanced diets and better manage their weight. Each of these tasks must be backed by concrete steps and levers. If these key tasks are carried out effectively, we will make solid progress in building a Healthy China. Third, strong institutional support should be provided to build a Healthy China This requires us to improve the working mechanism under which Party committees exercise overall leadership and Party and government departments work in tandem, refine the framework of policies and institutions for promoting people’s health, and make sure the principle of health promotion is embedded in the entire public policy process from formulation to implementation. We should deepen the reform of public hospitals and medical insurance payment models, improve the drug pricing mechanism, refine centralized procurement policies for medicines and medical consumables, ensure efficient use of medical insurance funds, and enhance the mechanisms for promoting coordinated development and governance of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals. We should encourage the application of scientific and technological advances in the health sector and use digital and intelligent technologies to improve public health. Moreover, we should strengthen Party organizations in the health sector, keep healthcare workers motivated and spur their creativity, step up the training and development of healthcare professionals, promote sound ethics and professional conduct, and cultivate a culture of integrity across the medical profession. Building a Healthy China calls for broad participation from across society. The Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference should play its role as a specialized consultative body, conducting in-depth surveys and studies on relevant issues, both theoretical and practical, and putting forward targeted and effective suggestions. Members of the Chinese Peasants and Workers Democratic Party and the Jiusan Society, along with people working in the medicine and health sector and the social welfare and social security sector, should fully leverage their professional expertise to contribute their wisdom and energy to building a Healthy China. This is the main part of remarks made by General Secretary Xi Jinping on March 6, 2026, at a joint group meeting of members of the Chinese Peasants and Workers Democratic Party, the Jiusan Society, the medicine and health sector, and the social welfare and social security sector at the fourth session of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference. (Originally appeared in Qiushi Journal, Chinese edition, No. 15, 2026)

item.title: Xi meets president of Swiss Confederation, calling for more certainty for China-Europe economic, trade cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Xi meets president of Swiss Confederation, calling for more certainty for China-Europe economic, trade cooperation Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin, who is paying a working visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. [Xinhua/Li Xiang] BEIJING -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin in Beijing on Friday, calling on both countries to inject confidence and more certainty into China-Europe economic and trade cooperation as well as into the global economic development. Noting Switzerland is an important partner of China in Europe, Xi said Swiss cooperation with China has always been at the forefront among European countries. He added that free trade cooperation has become the brightest highlight of China-Switzerland relations, which fully demonstrates the political courage and responsibility of the two countries in adhering to open cooperation, and highlights the unique leading role of both sides in promoting the building of an open world economy. China is willing to work with Switzerland to uphold openness, strengthen cooperation, promote a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and jointly inject confidence and more certainty into the economic and trade cooperation between China and European countries, as well as into the global economic development, Xi said. Since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China and Switzerland have continuously translated the China-Switzerland cooperation spirit, featuring equality, innovation and win-win results, into pragmatic outcomes, setting a model for interactions between countries of different sizes and with different social systems, Xi pointed out. He said the two sides should respect each other, treat each other as equals, and comprehensively enhance exchanges and policy alignment at different levels. Noting that China is accelerating the development of new quality productive forces and steadily expanding institutional opening up, Xi said the country is ready to turn its market into a market for the world and a shared market for all. Both sides should adhere to mutual benefit and win-win results, strengthen innovation cooperation and focus on fostering cooperation in emerging industries, including digital economy, green energy storage and artificial intelligence, he added. Xi expressed hope that Switzerland would leverage its unique influence to actively promote balanced and stable development of trade between China and European countries. As China and Switzerland share similar positions and concepts in supporting multilateralism, Xi said both sides should deepen multilateral coordination and mutual support, firmly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law, reform and improve the global governance system, and advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Parmelin said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, Switzerland and China have always respected each other, maintained close high-level exchanges, and achieved fruitful cooperation results in many fields such as trade and investment, scientific research and innovation, and employment. Noting that this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of Switzerland-China innovative strategic partnership, Parmelin said that the two sides have successfully completed negotiations on signing a protocol on upgrading free trade agreement in a short period of time with high quality, demonstrating a high level of mutual trust between the two sides, which will inject new impetus into bilateral relations. Switzerland firmly adheres to the one-China policy and looks forward to strengthening dialogue and exchanges with China, upholding mutually beneficial cooperation, and promoting greater development in cooperation in various fields, he said. The Swiss side attaches great importance to the positive role played by China in international affairs and is willing to closely coordinate with China, adhere to multilateralism, safeguard free trade, and contribute to world development, prosperity, peace and stability, Parmelin added. After their meeting, the two leaders witnessed the signing of the protocol on upgrading free trade agreement and multiple cooperation documents in areas like scientific research, employment and the media. Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin, who is paying a working visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. [Xinhua/Ding Lin]

item.title: Xi holds talks with German president, calls for opening new chapter in all-round strategic partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Xi holds talks with German president, calls for opening new chapter in all-round strategic partnership Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and his wife Elke Budenbender prior to the talks between Xi and Steinmeier at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. Xi held talks with Steinmeier, who is on a state visit to China, in Beijing on Friday. [Xinhua/Shen Hong] BEIJING -- Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Beijing on Friday, saying China is ready to work with Germany to open a new chapter in China-Germany all-round strategic partnership and promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system. Xi said as the world's second and third largest economies, China and Germany bear significant responsibilities for the development of China-EU relations and the stable growth of the world economy. Xi called on both sides to enhance communication and collaboration, create a new model of cooperation featuring equality, mutual benefit and strategic stability, and send out positive signals to the world of choosing openness over isolation and cooperation over confrontation. China's policy toward Germany is consistent, stable and predictable, and China is happy to see Germany play a greater role in European and international affairs, Xi said, noting that China has attached great importance to Germany's status as a major country and always supported its reunification and development. Xi expressed hope that Germany will view China's development and its cooperation with China with an open and positive attitude, uphold a rational, pragmatic and friendly policy toward China, and adhere to mutual respect and equal treatment, which is a valuable piece of experience for the sustained and sound development of China-Germany relations. Noting that Germany is a representative of advanced manufacturing and high-quality products, while China is advancing its modernization through high-quality development, Xi said the two sides have compatible development strategies and broad space for cooperation. Xi said China welcomes enterprises from Germany and other countries to deepen their presence in China and share the benefit of its supersized market. It is hoped that the German side will provide a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment for Chinese enterprises operating in Germany, he added. Xi expressed China's willingness to cooperate with Germany in areas such as artificial intelligence, green and low-carbon development, trade in services and digital economy to jointly enhance future competitiveness. Both sides should support cultural, educational and artistic exchanges, facilitate personnel exchanges, foster people-to-people connectivity, and create a favorable atmosphere for celebrating the 55th anniversary of bilateral ties next year, Xi said. China has always viewed the EU as a partner, and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and goodwill, said Xi, adding that history and reality have repeatedly shown that for China and the EU, cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences. He added that as long as both China and the EU stay committed to the positioning of their partnership and maintain the tone of equal-footed dialogue, differences and problems can be resolved and will not hinder further development of China-EU relations. It is hoped that the EU will work with China in the same direction to jointly advance an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, Xi said. Xi briefed Steinmeier on the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, adding that the CPC is willing to exchange governance experience with major political parties around the world, including those in Germany. Steinmeier, who is on a state visit to China, said that over the past 25 years, he has visited China eight times. Hailing China's rapid development, Steinmeier said China has become a major country with considerable political influence as well as economic, scientific and technological strength. Germany greatly admires the tremendous development achievements China has made under the leadership of President Xi, he noted. Germany firmly adheres to the one-China policy and is fully confident about the prospects of bilateral relations, Steinmeier said. The two countries can properly resolve economic and trade differences via dialogue and consultation to achieve win-win results, setting an example for the world, he said. Noting that the international order is under strain, and the world expects China to play a bigger role, Steinmeier said Germany is ready to jointly shoulder the responsibility of safeguarding world peace and development with China, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and the authority of international law, support free trade and WTO rules, and oppose protectionism and trade wars. Prior to the talks, Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan held a welcoming ceremony for Steinmeier and his wife Elke Büdenbender at the square outside the east entrance of the Great Hall of the People. Xi and Peng also held a welcoming banquet for Steinmeier and Büdenbender on Friday evening. item.title: Xi stresses Party self-governance to ensure CPC remains strong leadership core
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Xi stresses Party self-governance to ensure CPC remains strong leadership core BEIJING -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, stressed the need to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance to ensure that the CPC remains the strong leadership core in advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xi made the remarks at a symposium on Aug. 21 to solicit opinions from non-Party personages on drafting the resolution of the CPC Central Committee on certain major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The resolution was adopted at the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing. Addressing the symposium, Xi said that to govern the country well, the Party must first govern itself well, and to make the country strong, the Party must first strengthen itself. Wang Huning, Cai Qi and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, attended the symposium. The chairpersons of the central committees of the eight non-CPC parties, the chairperson of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce (ACFIC) and a representative of personages without party affiliation shared their views and suggestions, and expressed full support for the draft resolution. The CPC has unswervingly promoted full and rigorous Party self-governance since its 18th National Congress in 2012, and thus grown stronger through revolutionary tempering, Xi said. At the same time, he added, profound changes in global, national and Party conditions have brought new circumstances and issues to the endeavor to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance. It is essential to build firm confidence, maintain resolve and earnestly govern the Party well and build it stronger, he said. To persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance, it is important to make tenacious efforts to resolve prominent problems within the Party, Xi said. Efforts must be made to uphold and strengthen the CPC Central Committee's centralized, unified leadership, unwaveringly apply strict principles, improve the system of exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, and take strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle to advance Party building on all fronts, he said. At the symposium, Xi highlighted the need to uphold, develop and improve China's new type of political party system. He also expressed the hope that other political parties, the ACFIC and personages without party affiliation would stay committed to the original aspiration of multiparty cooperation, steadfastly uphold the leadership of the CPC, actively make proposals on state affairs, and give full play to their function of democratic oversight.
